As of May 2026, Elon Musk was the most-followed person on X (formerly Twitter), with 239.9 million followers. Additionally, former U.S. President Barack Obama amassed 119.4 million followers on the micro-blogging service. In April 2023, Musk changed Twitter's legal name to X Corp.

## Celebrities and Twitter

Founded in 2006 as Twitter, X is an online social networking and microblogging service that allows standard users to post text-based status updates and messages of up to 280 characters in length (the premium version does not have the limitation). X provides a near-instant access channel to celebrities. The majority of the top ten most-followed X accounts are entertainers who use the medium to communicate with fans, spread relevant news regarding their work, or work on their public image. The near-instant gratification through a stream of direct updates from celebrities or personalities as well as the feeling of belonging to a particular group of fans is a popular reason for social media users to use X. In order to establish authenticity of identity on X, accounts of people from high-interest areas such as music, fashion, entertainment, politics, media, business or other areas as well as individuals at high risk of impersonation are verified by X. The verification badge symbolizes that the account is maintained by a legitimate source. Major sporting events and industry award shows such as the Super Bowl, the Grammy Awards, or the Academy Awards generate lots of online buzz on X. The online discussion allows users to participate in the success of celebrities who often post behind-the-scenes photo tweets or commentaries. On-set or in-concert tweets are further methods of celebrities enhancing their appeal and level of fan interaction.

## X/Twitter accounts with the most followers: The top 10

Elon Musk currently has the most followers on X/Twitter.* Here’s a breakdown of the full top 10.

### 1. Elon Musk – 240.3 million followers

It makes sense that Elon Musk is the most-followed X/Twitter account — he bought the platform in 2022, and is the person behind the rebrand. Celebrated for driving companies like Tesla and SpaceX into the public eye, he’s now equally famous for controversial X posts and public speaking.

Musk’s brief position in the US government gave his posts extra sway with users, regardless of their opinion on the man himself. All of this makes him the only X/Twitter account with more than 200 million followers.

Big upgrade to@CommunityNotes https://t.co/YJWgNr07f8

> — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) February 6, 2026

### 2. Barack Obama – 119.2 million followers

Social media seems like second nature nowadays, but in 2008, Barack Obama was something of a trailblazer. The former US president was the first major candidate to use platforms like X/Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube during campaign season, lending him a more relatable vibe.

He still posts political content, but Obama’s feed covers everything from the Super Bowl to intimate snaps with his family. And of course, amid all the end-of-year lists, he’ll always share his favorite music, books, and films.

Black History Month is a time to recognize the lived, shared experience of all Black folks who have fundamentally shaped, challenged, and ultimately strengthened America. It’s about taking an unvarnished look at the past so that we can create a better future. As we mark 100 years… pic.twitter.com/WLZ5EpHK1K

> — Barack Obama (@BarackObama) February 1, 2026

### 3. Donald Trump – 111.6 million followers

Despite owning his own social media platform, Donald Trump is still the third-most-followed person on X/Twitter. After his second impeachment, the current US president’s account was suspended by X/Twitter’s old leadership. He was reinstated once Musk bought the company in 2022, and continues to post statements, updates, and press conferences.

It was great being with King Charles, Queen Camilla, and the Royal Family! pic.twitter.com/XFxJAH7aF2

> — Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) October 1, 2025

### 4. Cristiano Ronaldo – 109.9 million followers

Cristiano Ronaldo is the second-most followed account and most-followed person on Instagram— fourth place on X/Twitter isn’t too bad at all. The Portuguese footballer publishes a healthy mix of personal content, training footage, and sponsored posts, mirroring the range of his Instagram presence.

💛💙 pic.twitter.com/Pn4WaVrqcN

> — Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) February 4, 2026

### 5. Narendra Modi – 106.9 million followers

Narendra Modi has been the Indian prime minister for 12 years, securing a third term in 2024. Similar to Trump, the controversial politician has faced legal action, and is currently battling a lawsuit from X/Twitter. Posting in both English and Gujarati, Modi’s X/Twitter feed is largely populated with photo ops and snippets from press conferences.

A wonderful discussion with students on approaching exams with confidence and positivity. Do watch this very special episode of Pariksha Pe Charcha!#ParikshaPeCharcha26 https://t.co/k7IN79qvek

> — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) February 6, 2026

### 6. Rihanna – 97.4 million followers

Singer. Businesswoman. Actor. Whether you know Rihanna for Umbrella, Fenty Beauty, or shooting aliens in Battleship, the Barbadian superstar is one of the most-followed X/Twitter users because she keeps busy.

Rihanna’s X/Twitter activity is focused and business-driven, but genuine. You’ll find a heavy smattering of Fenty Beauty content mixed with magazine shoots, personal snaps, and behind-the-scenes clips. Whenever that new album eventually drops, we’re sure she’ll pick up a new follower or two.

my 2016 post winshappy ANTIversary 🙏🏿🎈⏳ pic.twitter.com/zzOgIPst2S

> — Rihanna (@rihanna) January 29, 2026

### 7. NASA – 92.1 million followers

The seventh entry in this list is the only agency or business. The name“NASA” is synonymous with exploration, adventure, and innovation — it’s the catch-all space research program, and its inclusion here is testament to that fact. SpaceX, owned by Musk, has roughly 50 million fewer followers.

Applications for the 2026 summer session close on Feb. 27. Explore our opportunities: https://t.co/xmq93hoBql pic.twitter.com/rYlQPrkdrD

> — NASA (@NASA) February 5, 2026

### 8. Justin Bieber – 90.7 million followers

If you weren’t there, it’s hard to understand just how massive Justin Bieber was back in the day. The Canadian singer made history with Baby, dividing music fans and securing the title of most-disliked YouTube video of all time. He was literally 15 at the time.

Since then, Bieber’s released multiple studio albums, relentlessly toured the world, and managed to shake off the unfair “guilty pleasure” tag that came with Baby.

Following a Ramsay Hunt syndrome diagnosis in 2022, he didn’t post anything on the platform for three years. He returned in July 2025 to promote his new album, Swag.

> — Justin Bieber (@justinbieber) January 29, 2026

### 9. Katy Perry – 87.3 million followers

Katy Perry may be ninth on this list, but she was the first person to reach 100 million followers back in 2017. The Firework hit-maker’s come a long way since her Warped Tour days, establishing herself as an American Idol judge and UNICEF ambassador.

Perry’s X/Twitter account goes hard on the business front, plugging upcoming gigs with a wink and a smile — she’s got tickets to sell, after all. But her feed always appears upbeat and colorful, mirroring the artwork and music videos that made her name.

Mummy’s home ✨♥️ pic.twitter.com/UxG9fB78Fn

> — KATY PERRY (@katyperry) December 11, 2025

### 10. Taylor Swift – 81.1 million followers

Taylor Swift is arguably the biggest celebrity in the world right now, pop star or otherwise. It makes sense that she’s crashing into this list at number ten — she doesn’t post much, but when she does, the numbers are wild. It’s pretty much all music-related, and written in Swift’s voice. Given how much weight her fans give her words and actions, that counts for a lot.

Twitter has changed. Or should we say X?

Whether you’re a brand, creator, or social media strategist, understanding how this fast-paced platform is evolving in 2026 is non-negotiable. From shifting user demographics and ad trends to engagement metrics that really matter, there’s a lot happening behind the scenes.

Numbers tell the full story. Here are 25+ X (Twitter) statistics that break down exactly how people use the platform, when they engage, who’s actually tuning in, and what’s working for businesses right now.

## Twitter Users Statistics — Key Data for 2026 Twitter Marketing

1. X (formerly Twitter) has approximately 557 million monthly active users worldwide in 2025, ranking as the 15th most-used social media platform globally. Despite being banned in China, the platform continues to maintain a strong global presence for real-time news, conversations, and brand engagement. [Statista X Users]

2. X.com ranks among the world’s most-visited websites, recording around 3.8 billion monthly visits, an average of 9.29 pages per visit, and a 46.28% bounce rate (November 2025 data). These metrics highlight strong web activity mostly desktop users, despite most users primarily accessing the platform via mobile apps. [Semrush X.com analytics]

3. The top 10 most-followed accounts on X are led by Elon Musk, followed by political figures and global superstars:

| Account | Handle | Followers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elon Musk | @elonmusk | ~230M |
| Barack Obama | @BarackObama | ~118M |
| Donald Trump | @realDonaldTrump | ~111M |
| Narendra Modi | @narendramodi | ~106M |
| Cristiano Ronaldo | @Cristiano | ~105M |
| Rihanna | @rihanna | ~96M |
| Justin Bieber | @justinbieber | ~89M |
| NASA | @NASA | ~87M |
| Katy Perry | @katyperry | ~85M |
| Taylor Swift | @taylorswift13 | ~78M |

4. X reached 7.1% of the world’s total population in January 2025 based on its overall user base. Among people aged 13 and above, 9.1% used X globally. Excluding China (where the platform is blocked), the eligible adoption rate increases to 11.2%. [DataReportal X Users]

X’s ad revenue grew for five consecutive quarters through early 2026, its longest sustained recovery since Elon Musk’s 2022 acquisition. [eMarketer]

## Twitter Demographics Stats

5. X’s user base is predominantly male, with men accounting for approximately 63.7% of users globally and women 36.3%. In the United States, about 63% of users are men (February 2025). [Statista X user distribution]

6. As of October 2025, the United States remains the largest market for X with approximately 99.04 million active users, followed by Japan with 71.19 million. Indonesia and India follow with 22.92 million and 22.17 million users respectively, while the UK records about 18.96 million. [Statista X Global Audience]

7. X’s income distribution in the United States (Pew Research 2025):

- 16% of users from households earning less than $30K/year
- 19% from $30K–$69,999
- 26% from $70K–$99,999
- 25% from households earning $100K or more

This highlights X’s skew toward middle- and higher-income adults. [Pew Research Center]

8. The majority of X users are under 35, with approximately 51.95% of the platform’s total audience aged 18–34. Adults aged 25–34 represent the single largest age group on the platform. [Statista US X users age]

9. According to Pew Research’s 2025 survey, X users in the US are spread across: 23% in urban areas, 22% in suburban communities, and 17% in rural areas, indicating the platform reaches audiences across diverse living environments. [Pew Research Center]

10. Politically, 24% of Republicans report using X compared with 19% of Democrats, a notable reversal from 2023, when Democrats were more likely to use the platform (26% vs. 20%). [Pew Research Center]

## Twitter Usage and Engagement Statistics

11. According to Pew Research Center’s 2025 survey, 21% of US adults report using X, making it the eighth most-used social media platform among American adults. YouTube (84%), Facebook (71%), and Instagram (50%) lead in overall usage. [Pew Research Center]

12. About 10% of US adults use X daily — 6% several times a day and 4% about once a day. Platforms like Facebook and YouTube see much higher daily engagement. [Pew Research Center]

13. About 29% of internet users aged 16+ reported using X at least once in the past month. By comparison, Facebook led with 56.9%, followed by YouTube at 55.4% and Instagram at 55.1%. [DataReportal Global Overview]

14. Among active X users (aged 16+), 59.7% used the platform to keep up with news and current events, the highest of any platform for that purpose. 38.1% followed or researched brands and products, 35.7% looked for entertaining content, 28.3% posted photos and videos, and 19.4% messaged friends and family. [DataReportal Global Overview]

15. On average, people spend about 16 minutes per visit on X, with total daily time adding up to 28 minutes (global average) and the US average at 34 minutes. Most users visit multiple times a day. [Semrush X Overview& Statista SM Daily Uses]

16. Engagement across all post formats on X has been declining. Average likes per post fell from 37.82 (2023) to 31.46 (2024). Mentions dropped from 11.06 to 8.47, while reposts declined sharply from 4.1 to 1.56. [Statista X Avg Engagement]

17. Engagement declined across all major platforms in 2025, but X experienced the steepest drop at 48%. Facebook followed at -36%, TikTok -34%, and Instagram -16%. [RivalIQ Benchmark Report]

18. According to RivalIQ, most industries post under 8 tweets per week with engagement below 0.04%. Sports Teams stand out, posting 40–50 times per week and achieving engagement around 0.07%. [RivalIQ Benchmark Report]

## Twitter Business Statistics

19. According to eMarketer’s forecast, X is projected to post its first year of ad revenue growth since Elon Musk’s 2022 acquisition. US ad sales are estimated to increase 17.5% to $1.31 billion in 2025, while global ad revenue is forecast to rise 16.5% to $2.26 billion and Q1 2026 quarterly revenue reached approximately $752 million, up ~17% year-over-year. [eMarketer X Ad Revenue]

20. X is used by 55.8% of brands for social media marketing, with 31.3% of B2B marketers ranking it among their top platforms for impact, according to HubSpot’s Social Media Marketing Report. For lead generation, LinkedIn dominates with over 80% of B2B social media leads, while X contributes approximately 12%, per Oktopost’s analysis of 100,000+ posts. [HubSpot/ Oktopost]

21. Kantar data shows that 26% of marketers plan to reduce ad spending on X in 2025, the largest planned cut among any major global ad platform. Trust in advertising on X has dropped from 22% in 2022 to 12% in 2024. Only 4% of marketers believe ads on X offer strong brand safety, compared with 39% for Google. [Kantar Media Reactions 2024]

22. X have about 6.3 million active paid subscribers as of March 31, 2026 with 4.4 million for X and 1.9 million for Grok. [DigitalApplied]

23. X now accounts for approximately 0.2% of total global digital ad spend, compared with Facebook’s 14.6% and TikTok’s 7.1%, underscoring the scale gap between X and the leading platforms for advertisers. [eMarketer SM Ad Spending]

## Twitter Ad & Marketing Statistics

24. On X, mobile devices drive 58.26% of traffic compared to 41.74% from desktops, a strong mobile-first audience that underscores the importance of mobile-optimized creatives. [Semrush X.com analytics]

25. X has an advertising audience of approximately 550 million people worldwide, equivalent to 10.5% of all internet users. While smaller than Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok, X’s real-time, interest-driven communities offer brands meaningful reach. [DataReportal / Kepios]

26. X users are 76% more open to trying new things, check the platform 16+ times daily, and are 45% more likely to click on ads than users on other platforms. [X Advertising]

27. About 89% of users on X use the platform to discover new products, and 76% say conversations they see there influence their purchase decisions. [X for Business]

28. Vertical Video Ads are the fastest-growing ad format on X, accounting for approximately 20% of total daily user time. Users are 7 times more likely to interact (follow, repost, like, or click) with Vertical Video Ads than with the same ads in the Home Timeline. [X Advertising]

29. The average engagement rate for an X influencer post is 0.09%. Video posts far outperform this at 0.42%, while text posts average 0.10% and photo posts 0.08%, confirming that video drives the most interaction. [Sprout Social Influencer Marketing Report]

30. Grok, X’s integrated AI assistant built by xAI, reached approximately 17.8% of the US AI chatbot market share in January 2026, up from just 1.9% in January 2025. [Reuters ]

## How to Turn Twitter (X) Stats Into a Smarter Strategy

Twitter (X) statistics reveal how people discover content, engage with brands, and make buying decisions. Use these insights to create smarter strategies that improve visibility, engagement, and results.

Here’s how businesses can use X statistics effectively:

### 1. Real-time news is X’s primary use case: Build content around it

59.7% of active X users are there specifically for news and current events, the highest of any platform for that purpose. For brands, this means timely commentary on industry developments, product launches aligned to trending topics, and fast-response customer engagement matter more on X than on any other platform.

### 2. Engagement is low but qualified

The 0.09% average influencer engagement rate sounds low, but X’s users are highly intentional. 76% say conversations on X influence their purchases, and 89% use it to discover new products. Smaller audience, stronger intent.

### 3. Video is the only format bucking the engagement decline

Engagement across all X post formats has been falling, but vertical video is X’s fastest-growing ad format. Users are 7x more likely to interact with Vertical Video Ads than with the same content in the Home Timeline. Video posts achieve 0.42% influencer engagement, nearly 5x the platform average.

### 4. Ad confidence is low, but recovering

Kantar’s data shows significant planned ad spend cuts on X through 2024–2025. But eMarketer’s forecasts show growth returning: US ad revenue up 17.5% in 2025, Q1 2026 up ~17% year-over-year. Brands re-entering X are finding lower CPM competition and a small-business advertiser base that’s been building steadily since 2023.

### 5. Political skew is now Republican-leaning

In 2025, 24% of Republicans use X versus 19% of Democrats, a reversal from two years prior. For brands marketing to politically aware audiences or managing brand safety concerns, this demographic shift is worth building into platform strategy and creative tone decisions.

Conclusion

Twitter may have evolved into X, but its role in real-time conversations, news, and brand engagement remains as relevant as ever. The platform continues to shift from changing user demographics and ad recovery to declining engagement and the rise of video-first content. For marketers, success on X in 2026 means understanding where attention is moving and adapting strategies accordingly.

# Twitter Statistics 2026: Must-Know Growth Data

Last updated on: March 27, 2026

Twitter (now widely known as X) remains one of the most influential platforms for real-time communication, shaping how people consume news, engage with brands, and participate in global conversations. From breaking political developments and financial market updates to customer service interactions and viral trends, the platform plays a critical role across industries such as media, marketing, and public relations.

Businesses use it to manage brand reputation and drive engagement, while journalists and creators rely on it for instant reach and visibility. As user behavior shifts and new features emerge, understanding the latest statistics becomes essential for making informed decisions. Let’s explore the latest Twitter statistics to understand how the platform is evolving.

## Editor’s Choice

- Twitter (X) has approximately 561 million monthly active users (MAUs) globally in 2026.
- The platform recorded around 245 million daily active users (DAUs) in 2026.
- The United States leads with over 105 million users, making it the largest market.
- Twitter’s monthly users declined by about 4.27% from 2025 to 2026.
- Around 60.6% of users use Twitter for news and current affairs.
- Roughly 34.9% of users research brands and products on the platform.
- Twitter generates about $2.5 billion in annual revenue (2024), with most coming from ads.

## Recent Developments

- Twitter rebranded to X and continues expanding into an “everything app” model with payments and AI features.
- The platform’s MAUs dropped from 586 million in 2025 to 561 million in 2026, signaling consolidation.
- Tweet activity increased, with posting volume rising by 8% year-over-year.
- Engagement actions such as shares grew by 35% between 2024 and 2025.
- Overall engagement value increased by 19% despite lower reach, indicating stronger interactions.
- Twitter’s workforce reduction after the acquisition impacted operations, with over 6,000 layoffs reported.
- Monetization features like subscriptions and creator tools expanded significantly in 2025–2026.
- Mobile daily users declined by 15.2% year-over-year, suggesting a shift in usage patterns.
- Competing platforms like Threads reached 115 million daily users by 2025, increasing competition.

## Twitter Overview and Key Stats

- Twitter ranks 15th among global social platforms by user base.
- The platform has an estimated 557–570 million active users, depending on methodology.
- Around 44% of users are daily active, showing strong retention.
- Twitter’s ad-supported users (mDAU) are approximately 237–245 million globally.
- The platform receives over 4.4 billion monthly website visits, making it one of the most visited sites.
- Twitter is used by 3.2% of global social media users as their favorite platform.
- Around 88.1% of Twitter users also use Instagram, highlighting cross-platform behavior.
- Approximately 81% of users also use Facebook and YouTube, reinforcing multi-platform engagement.

## Top Twitter Accounts by Followers: Key Insights

- Elon Musk dominates the platform with 234.2 million followers, holding a massive lead over all other accounts.
- Barack Obama ranks second with 119.2 million followers, trailing Musk by over 115 million, highlighting a significant gap at the top.
- Donald Trump secures the third position with 110.7 million followers, maintaining a strong influence on the platform.
- Narendra Modi is the most-followed Indian account with 106.1 million followers, ranking 4th globally.
- Cristiano Ronaldo, the only sportsperson in the top 5, has 105.5 million followers, showing the global appeal of sports personalities.
- Among entertainers, Rihanna leads with 96.3 million followers, followed by Justin Bieber (89.8 million) and Katy Perry (85.1 million).
- NASA, with 88.6 million followers, stands out as the only organization in the top 10, reflecting strong public interest in space and science.
- Taylor Swift closes the top 10 with 78.8 million followers, still maintaining a massive fan base.
- The top 5 accounts all exceed 100 million followers, indicating an elite tier of global influence on Twitter (X).
- There is a sharp drop after rank 1, with Elon Musk having nearly double the followers of the second-ranked account, emphasizing his unmatched reach on the platform.

Reference: DemandSage

## Total Twitter Users Worldwide

- Twitter has about 561 million monthly active users globally in 2026.
- The platform recorded around 557 million users in 2025, showing a slight decline.
- Some estimates suggest a peak of 600 million users in 2025 before a decline.
- Twitter had just 40 million users in 2010, reflecting massive long-term growth.
- The platform crossed 300 million users in 2015, marking early mainstream adoption.
- The global user base declined by nearly 7.84% between 2023 and 2024.
- Twitter remains among platforms with over 500 million users, alongside Reddit and Threads.
- Estimates suggest a fluctuation range between 550M to 600M users due to reporting differences.

## Monthly Active Users Statistics

- Twitter’s MAU count stands at 561 million in 2026.
- The platform had 586 million MAUs in 2025, indicating a decline.
- In 2024, MAUs were estimated at around 388 million, showing reporting variation.
- Some sources estimate 570 million MAUs in early 2026, depending on methodology.
- Twitter experienced year-over-year growth of 7% in 2025 before stabilizing.
- MAU growth slowed significantly after 2022, reflecting market maturity.
- The platform’s ad reach also aligns closely with MAU at around 557 million users.
- Monthly usage remains stable despite competition from newer platforms.

## Daily Active Users Statistics

- Twitter has approximately 245 million daily active users globally.
- Daily users account for roughly 44% of total monthly users.
- Some estimates place DAU as high as 259 million in 2026, showing moderate growth.
- Monetizable daily active users (mDAU) stand at around 237.8 million.
- Twitter reported about 200 million daily users in 2024, indicating growth.
- Mobile daily active users are estimated at 132 million globally.
- DAU growth has stabilized post-2023 despite platform changes.
- Daily engagement remains high due to news consumption and trending topics.

## X (Twitter) Growth Over the Years

- X’s user base grew from 310 million in 2017 to 561 million in 2026, reflecting a long-term upward trajectory despite short-term fluctuations.
- The platform experienced an initial dip in 2018, dropping to 298 million users, before recovering steadily in subsequent years.
- Between 2019 and 2023, X saw consistent growth, rising from 312 million to 421 million users, indicating strong adoption and engagement during this period.
- A notable acceleration occurred between 2020 and 2022, where users increased from 347 million to 401 million, marking a gain of 54 million users in just two years.
- In 2024, the platform experienced a decline to 388 million users, signaling a temporary slowdown or user churn phase.
- The most significant surge came in 2025, when X’s user base jumped to 586 million, representing the highest level in the dataset and a sharp year-over-year increase.
- However, 2026 shows a slight decline to 561 million users, suggesting a correction phase after rapid growth.
- Overall, despite periodic dips, X demonstrates a net growth of +251 million users from 2017 to 2026, highlighting its continued relevance in the global social media landscape.

Reference: Statista

## Time Spent and Usage Frequency

- Users spend an average of 31 minutes per day on Twitter.
- The average session duration is around 10–11 minutes per visit.
- About 42% of users check Twitter daily, reflecting habitual usage.
- Nearly 25% of users log in multiple times per day, especially for news updates.
- The platform sees peak usage during morning and evening hours, aligning with commute times.
- Users follow an average of 400+ accounts, increasing feed consumption.
- Around 70% of users consume content passively, without posting frequently.
- Only about 10% of users generate 80% of tweets, showing content concentration.

## Twitter Traffic and Visits Statistics

- Twitter receives over 4.4 billion monthly website visits globally.
- The United States contributes nearly 25% of total web traffic.
- Average monthly visits per user are estimated at 12–14 sessions.
- Mobile accounts for over 80% of total traffic, showing mobile dominance.
- Desktop traffic makes up about 20% of visits, mostly for professional use.
- Bounce rates average around 38–42%, indicating moderate engagement.
- Users view an average of 6–7 pages per session, depending on region.
- Referral traffic from news sites contributes significantly during major events.
- Organic search accounts for a small share, under 10% of total traffic.

## X (Twitter) Users by Age Group: Key Insights

- The 25–34 age group dominates X (Twitter), accounting for 29.62% of total users, making it the platform’s largest demographic.
- Close behind, 18–24-year-olds represent 27.39%, reinforcing that X has a strong young adult user base.
- Combined, users aged 18–34 make up 57.01% of the platform, meaning over half of X’s audience is under 35.
- The 35–44 age group contributes 17.91%, showing a significant but smaller mid-age user segment.
- Older demographics decline steadily, with 45–54 users at 11.74% and 55–64 users at 8.03%.
- The 65+ age group represents just 5.03%, making it the smallest segment on the platform.
- Overall, the data highlights that X (Twitter) is heavily skewed toward younger audiences, making it ideal for targeting Gen Z and Millennials.

Reference: Resourcera

## Web vs Mobile Usage Statistics

- Over 80% of X users access the platform via mobile devices.
- Mobile accounts for 55% of X website visits, desktop 45%.
- Desktop users spend more time per session than mobile users.
- iOS users show higher engagement and are 28% more likely to subscribe than Android users.
- Mobile notifications drive 54% of re-engagement on X.
- 61% of journalists use X daily, favoring desktop access.
- 89% of X usage occurs on mobile devices.
- Mobile users spend 34% more time per session compared to desktop users.
- Push notifications boost 7-day retention by 31%.

## Tweet Volume and Posting Trends

- Twitter users post around 500 million tweets per day globally.
- That equals approximately 6,000 tweets per second.
- Tweet volume increased by 8% year-over-year in 2025, indicating active participation.
- The average user posts about 2–3 tweets per week, depending on engagement level.
- Around 80% of tweets come from 10% of users, highlighting power users.
- Tweets with hashtags receive 33% more engagement than those without.
- Visual tweets (images/videos) generate 150% more engagement than text-only posts.
- The average tweet length remains under 280 characters, with most under 100 characters.
- Trending topics drive spikes in tweet volume during major global events.

## User Reactions to the New X (Twitter) Logo

- The majority of users feel neutral (33.57%), indicating a wait-and-watch approach toward the rebranding.
- Around 24.4% of users reacted positively, showing moderate acceptance of the new X logo.
- A notable 22.39% of users reported confusion, highlighting uncertainty and lack of clarity around the brand shift.
- Meanwhile, 19.64% expressed negative sentiment, suggesting resistance or dissatisfaction with the new identity.

- Replies and conversations have increased by 35% year-over-year.
- Poll tweets achieve 20% higher interaction rates compared to standard tweets.
- Tweets posted during peak hours (8–10 AM and 6–9 PM) gain significantly higher engagement.
- Accounts that tweet consistently (daily) see 2x more engagement growth than irregular accounts.
- Brand tweets receive an average of 1–3 interactions per 1,000 followers, depending on industry.

## Twitter Algorithm and Reach Statistics

- The X algorithm tests new tweets with a small audience, ranking about 1,500 candidate tweets per refresh based on predicted engagement.
- Engagement velocity in the first 30–60 minutes is a top signal, with above-average early responses triggering large reach expansion.
- Tweets more than 24 hours old rarely receive major algorithmic distribution unless they get a sudden reshare boost from big accounts.
- The “For You” feed uses interest predictions and high engagement to drive a majority of tweet impressions for many users.
- Tweets with images get about 150% more retweets than text-only posts, strongly boosting their chances in algorithmic feeds.
- Hashtag use makes tweets roughly 33% more likely to be retweeted, improving their ranking and visibility.
- The algorithm evaluates thousands of features and predicts probabilities for about 10 engagement types (likes, replies, follows, etc.) for each tweet.
- Reply–to–reply exchanges can carry up to a 75x higher algorithmic value than simple likes, massively amplifying reach.
- Threads with external links have seen reduced reach after 2024 updates, while threads with high bookmarks and subscriptions get extra weight.

## Top Motivations for Using X (Twitter)

- News consumption dominates usage, with 60.6% of users using X to stay updated with the latest news and current affairs, making it the platform’s primary use case.
- Brand discovery is significant, as 34.9% of users rely on X to research new brands and products, highlighting its role in the purchase decision journey.

- Twitter Blue (premium subscription) adoption crossed 1 million users globally.
- Polls, threads, and long-form posts are increasingly used by creators and brands.

- Twitter generated approximately $2.5 billion in ad revenue in 2024, down from previous years.
- Advertising accounts for nearly 85–90% of total revenue.
- The average cost per engagement (CPE) ranges between $0.50 and $2.00, depending on campaign type.
- Promoted tweets can increase brand awareness by up to 70%.
- Video ads generate 2x higher recall rates compared to static ads.
- Twitter ads reach over 544 million users globally.
- Small businesses increasingly use Twitter ads, with adoption rising by 18% year-over-year.
- Subscription-based monetization (creators, premium features) is expanding steadily post-2023.

## Twitter Usage by Country and Region

- The United States has over 105 million Twitter users, the largest share globally.
- Japan ranks second with approximately 74 million users, showing strong regional adoption.
- India has over 27 million users, with steady growth in emerging markets.
- Brazil accounts for nearly 24 million users, driven by social engagement trends.
- The United Kingdom has around 23 million users, making it a key European market.
- Indonesia contributes about 18 million users, reflecting Southeast Asia’s growth.
- Approximately 80% of Twitter users are outside the US, highlighting global reach.
- North America contributes around 20% of total users, while Asia-Pacific dominates the user share.
- Europe accounts for roughly 15–18% of total users, depending on estimates.

## Twitter Competitors and Market Share

- X (Twitter) holds roughly 5.6–5.8% of the global social‑media market share as of early 2026.
- Facebook dominates with over 80% share of global social‑media traffic, far exceeding Twitter.
- Instagram commands about 4.9% market share, backed by more than 3 billion monthly active users.
- TikTok accounts for roughly 36% platform‑reach share and reaches around 1.99 billion users monthly.
- Threads has surged to roughly 4.5% share in some regional rankings, with over 400 million monthly active users.
- Reddit reaches about 0.77 billion monthly active users and holds a niche share in text‑based communities.
- LinkedIn claims roughly 21–22% of global social‑media platform reach, targeting professional audiences.
- YouTube holds about 5.0–5.5% market share, overlapping with Twitter in real‑time news and commentary.
- Snapchat and Pinterest each hover around 3% market share, competing for younger, visual‑first users.
- Despite competition, X (Twitter) remains in the top 15 most‑used social platforms worldwide based on traffic and engagement metrics.

## Future Outlook and Forecasts

- Twitter’s user base is expected to stabilize around 550–600 million users through 2027.
- Monetization will likely shift toward subscriptions, which could account for up to 30% of Twitter’s revenue by 2027.
- AI‑driven recommendations will play a larger role in content discovery, with over 70% of timelines forecast to be algorithmically curated by 2027.
- Short‑form video and live audio features are expected to grow significantly, with video consumption projected to rise by 15–20% annually through 2027.
- Advertising revenue may recover gradually, with projected growth of 5–8% annually, reaching around $7–8 billion by 2027.
- Emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia will drive user growth, contributing an estimated 40–50% of net new users by 2027.
- Competition from Threads and TikTok will influence feature innovation, with platforms expected to double short‑form video‑related features by 2027.
- Integration of payments and “super apps” features could redefine platform usage, with 20–25% of users projected to use in‑app payment or commerce tools by 2027.
- E‑commerce and creator‑driven sales on Twitter may reach $1–1.5 billion annually by 2027, driven by creator‑led campaigns.
- AI‑assisted content creation tools are expected to be adopted by over 60% of active creators on the platform by 2027, boosting engagement by up to 15%.

Twitter has around 557–561 million monthly active users globally in 2026.

Approximately 44–45% of Twitter users are daily active users (DAUs).

### How much has Twitter’s ad revenue declined since its peak?

Twitter’s ad revenue dropped by nearly 50–55% from around $5 billion to $2.5 billion after 2021.

## Conclusion

Twitter continues to evolve as a real-time communication platform, balancing user engagement with new monetization strategies and feature expansion. While overall user growth has slowed and competition from platforms like TikTok and Threads has intensified, Twitter still holds a unique position in delivering instant information and facilitating public discourse. Its strength lies in real-time updates, making it a preferred platform for news, live events, and direct brand-consumer interaction.

At the same time, the platform is undergoing a structural shift toward subscriptions, creator monetization, and AI-driven content discovery. These changes signal a move beyond traditional social networking into a broader digital ecosystem. For businesses, marketers, and content creators, adapting to these changes will be critical to maintaining visibility and engagement.

Overall, the data highlights a platform in transition, still highly relevant, but increasingly shaped by innovation, competition, and evolving user expectations.

## Why Follower Counts Aren’t Everything

At first glance, it’s tempting to think the more followers an account has, the more influential it must be. After all, Elon Musk’s 220 million or Barack Obama’s 130 million followers look like undeniable proof of clout. But here’s the catch: popularity doesn’t always translate to impact.

First, not all followers are actively engaged. A portion of those millions may be inactive users, bots, or casual onlookers who never interact with the content. What really drives influence on Twitter is engagement metrics the likes, retweets, comments, and quote tweets that show people are actively responding and participating in the conversation. An account with just 100,000 highly engaged followers can often outperform a celebrity account with 10 million passive ones.

Second, authenticity plays a major role. Users today crave genuine voices, not curated PR statements. That’s why some niche creators, journalists, or industry experts with modest followings have outsized influence. Their audiences trust them, seek their insights, and amplify their voices far beyond what follower counts suggest.

Third, algorithms matter. Twitter’s recommendation system favors tweets that drive conversations. This means an account with fewer followers but higher engagement can consistently appear in trending feeds, gaining visibility on par with celebrity accounts.

Finally, context is everything. For example, if you’re an entrepreneur, following an AI researcher with 50,000 followers might bring more value to your feed than a pop star with 100 million. Influence is relative it depends on who you are, what you’re looking for, and the communities you want to engage with.

In 2026, the smartest Twitter strategy isn’t chasing the biggest accounts but curating a feed that balances reach, relevance, and authenticity. It’s about building a digital space where you’re informed, entertained, and inspired not just impressed by big numbers.
